name: Sheep Sorrel
caution: The lemon tang is oxalic acid: a fine garnish and nibble, not a whole salad, and best skipped by those prone to kidney stones. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Small arrowhead leaves with backward-pointing lobes, low in lawns and poor soils. Pleasantly sour when you chew one.

sections.title: On the trail
sections.body: A bright wild lemon: scatter a few leaves over fish or into a salad for a jolt of sourness.
